utterances.text: Can you relate to the Court, please, other than this particular event that you've testified about in the last few minutes, during the two and a half weeks, approximately, that you were in custody, and concerning all the things you have told us about in your testimony, did you ever at any time see any other HVO soldiers or guards disciplined or punished or stopped in terms of anything that they were doing to the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not at all. No question of that. That was never written down in any act or document of the HVO, that anybody should be punished or disciplined for anything they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, on the morning of the 8th of February, 1993, you and some other of the Muslim prisoners were, in fact, gathered at Kaonik camp and exchanged and released on that day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At the time, the exchange was, in fact, delayed, as you told us a few minutes ago, because at least two, if not three, of the men who were already known to the Red Cross, had previously become known to the Red Cross, could not be found or identified at Kaonik on the 8th of February; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, because they were still at Kula, dead, so the exchange was two or three hours late, as far as I recall. But it nevertheless did take place ultimately.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct, sir, that present at the exchange on the 8th of February, 1993, were Zlatko Aleksovski, Anto Sliskovic, and Zarko Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: One moment. No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Naumovski?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Mr. J, let me introduce myself. My name is Mitko Naumovski, I am Defence counsel for Mr. Dario Kordic. It is standard practice to say at the beginning that as both of us can understand each other, I should like to ask you to make pauses between my questions and your answers so that this can be interpreted into the other languages. Thank you. Mr. J, I have some general questions for you to begin with. Before the war, you were a tradesman, you had a shop; what do you do now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I am a taxi driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, were you a member of the Party for Democratic Action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Throughout?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you have any particular duties in the SDA in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, on the 8th of February, 1993, you left Busovaca and went to Zenica, did you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I went to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you arrived in Zenica, were you assigned a position in the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, because for two whole months, up to the end of May, that is to say, almost three months, I was a man half dead. I was undergoing treatment. I could hardly move. So I had no call-up duties from the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Does that mean that you were not a soldier at all or only those few months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Up until May, I was not, but after that, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: May we agree then that after May 1993, you were a soldier in the 303rd Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So the answer is "Yes," if I understood you correctly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. The answer is "Yes."

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, whether, as a soldier, you went to the Busovaca municipality at all?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. I was at Kula as a soldier on the front line.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber when this was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: From May to the end of the war. I was even at the delineation line at Kula up until that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So if I have understood you correctly, this entire military service was done at the front line at Kula from May 1993 to the beginning of 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, Witness J, whether you were a member of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, when you became a member of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: In Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: How long were you a member of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Only two or three months, until -- that is to say, when, on the 9th of May, what happened happened, and perhaps ten days after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the Patriotic League in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: We didn't have any commanders. It was a group of some 30-odd young men and I was sometimes at the head of a group, we tried to organise something. We tried but, let us be clear on this point, that Patriotic League at that particular time, what it did, and in my testimony I mentioned Florijan Glavocevic, and it refers to where we talked and where we placed ourselves in the service of this, to do some good, to help as much as we could the HVO to be united in the defence, and allegedly there was the threat from the Yugoslav People's Army and from the Serbs, but we were not accepted by Mr. Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, we'll talk about Mr. Glavocevic later on. These are just in my introductory questions. But as you mentioned that, I'm going to -- you said alleged threat from the Serbs in the spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, alleged.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you consider that there was no threat from the Serbs when you say "alleged"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, not in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What about the broader area of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes. There, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, Witness J, as we just mentioned the Patriotic League, were you in Mehurici where they say the Patriotic League was founded for the area of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you would agree with me that the Patriotic League did have a certain setup, that is to say, lower units, and superior command, and so on and so forth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, we can call it that, but we did not have anyone who gives orders. Nobody gave us orders. We were primarily organised to help in the defence of Busovaca and to help prevent what, in fact, did occur later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I am interested to know what the paper you have in front of you is. You keep referring to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I can give it to you. They are the names of the persons who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Just tell us. That many be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, it just contains the names of the people who were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In Busovaca you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. When I asked you about the Patriotic League at the level of Central Bosnia, what I wanted to know was whether you had any contacts with Ibrahim Puric, who was the commander of the Patriotic League for Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, and I don't even know him to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When you spoke about the command of the Patriotic League in Busovaca, you said that for a time you were one of the sort of leaders of the group.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who was there after you or before you? Was there anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, after me -- I don't know who came after me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: For example, Dervis Sarajlic, was he there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. He was one of us, that is to say, one of those people who, in fact, led those 30 young men who to tried to do something and balance out the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: At that time, the time we're talking about, the soldiers of the Patriotic League, that is to say, the members that we're discussing now, where was their headquarters? Where did they do their training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, they didn't train anywhere, but their headquarters were in the fire brigade building in the centre of Busovaca, but they had no training at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Where did you say they had their headquarters? I'm sorry, I missed that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the fire brigade building.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. In the fire brigade building. But I'm not clear on your answer as to why you organised yourselves in Busovaca. To defend yourselves against whom at the beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, sir, the situation was so terrible and this was hovering in the air that we had to do something. We had to attempt to balance out and even out the situation, to try and do something, to try and do anything to prevent what happened from happening, but we did not succeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I did not understand something. To defend yourselves from whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, defence from whom. If you're going to -- how shall I put it? Defend ourselves from whom. That's a funny question. First of all --

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to ask you to answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, first of all, let's get this clear. That Patriotic League, that portion that was in Busovaca and which we set up on our own initiative without any orders from anybody or without consulting anybody from above, we did not know anything about that nor did we contact anyone. But we did try, first and foremost, to try to agree with the Croats and to have a sort of platform from which to talk, because we had no armed force available.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Perhaps I'm not understanding you properly, but did you answer the question? Who were you preparing to defend yourselves against?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, against the Serbs, of course, the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But a moment ago you said that they were the alleged enemy of you people in Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, when you look at the municipality of Busovaca today and the municipalities that surround the Busovaca municipality, it would be difficult to suppose that the threat came from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, I think that we'll agree that the former JNA bombed Busovaca in April. We need not suppose that. We agree that is something that occurred. So that is a direct attack.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, yes, direct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, within the context of these questions, did you have any weapons yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you have your own weapons or as a member of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I had my own weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Just make some pauses before you answer, please. What weapons did you have?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had a Scorpion pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: How many bullets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Twenty, thirty, depending on the charge, but not more than thirty.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, about the following -- I have several questions. I prepared my questions chronologically, according to your testimony, so we're going to stick to that order more or less. With respect to the handing out of weapons in the former barracks of the Busovaca municipality, did you have any duties in agreements between the SDA and HDZ about the distribution of those barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, none. None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Does that mean that you have no knowledge of the circumstances under which the Dragavoj barracks was allotted to the HVO and the barracks at Kacuni or in the Silos went to the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Under which circumstances? Well, it is easy to say. In the Silo there is a purely Muslim population and that is a fact. The HVO did not even attempt to take anything there. Whereas the events concerning the other two barracks, I have no information as to whom conducted the negotiations, whether there were any negotiations or what actually happened. I only know that when the weapons were taken from there, this was celebrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Croats celebrated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You're thinking about Kaonik, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Right. Now we're going to ask you a few questions about Kaonik. In connection with the weapons in Kaonik, were you a member of the team which negotiated the way in which the weapons would be distributed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you have no personal knowledge about that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Who was on the team, who negotiated, I have no idea, or whether they did at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you don't even know whether there were any negotiations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you said on Thursday that Dario Kordic was involved in this. So after all, you do have some knowledge about what happened, some direct knowledge.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: In those days and throughout that period of time, everything was under the leadership of Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: My question is specifically for Kaonik. Do you have any direct knowledge of the fact that Mr. Kordic was involved in planning the action that took place in Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know that exactly, whether he was directly involved or one of his men, but that is less important.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In view of the fact that you told Their Honours your own conclusion, would you please tell us the details and the basis on which you made that conclusion that he was involved in planning the operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Not a single event of any kind, any negotiations or anything that took place. Even children knew that only Dario Kordic was responsible, that everything was under his supervision.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Apart from this general answer that you have given us several times during your direct-examination as well, my question is: Regarding this specific event in Kaonik, do you have any direct knowledge of any particular detail from which you make your conclusion that Dario Kordic was involved in the planning of the operation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do not have a data about it. Let's say I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you don't have. Very well. Tell us, please, were you on the spot when this was happening at the Kaonik barracks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. Who could have been on the spot? We all had to be in our homes. We couldn't even move around properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: On the 9th of May, 1992, you were not allowed to move around?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: But there was a great power behind it. It was a show of might, of enormous might.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, how then did other Muslims -- how then were other Muslims present that evening when you were not allowed to move freely?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know at all that there was some skirmishes on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I heard about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You heard about it, but you have no direct knowledge?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But what you heard goes against what you just said, that you were not allowed to move in 1992. A Muslim who was wounded, I think his name was Mesic, was there with his lorry, for example, yet you are claiming that there was no freedom of movement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Upon whose orders and on the basis of what agreement he was present, I don't know, but clearly if he was there then he must have been in agreement with someone, but I have no knowledge about that, why they were there or how.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps, that Dervis Sarajlic was there too?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has said these are purely things which he heard and, as such, the evidence isn't going to assist us very much. So if we could move on, please, Mr. Naumovski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Today, Witness J, you frequently used the term "HVO." Allow me to clear that up a little. When you say the "HVO," what exactly do you mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: The Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but as an army, a military force, or in some other sense?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: As a military force, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Witness J, do you know that in Busovaca municipality, as in other municipalities, the HVO had its civilian component that was also called HVO but that represented the civilian authority?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably, yes, but I did not see the effects of those civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that HVO civilian authority existed in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: The civilian authorities did exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: A moment ago you said or, rather, in answer to a question about Florijan Glavocevic, you said that he was a president of a war council but so such body existed, I think.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think it was called something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But if you had said he was president of the HVO, that would be understandable, but no war council. That didn't exist.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, it did. Yes, it did. A war council did exist in Busovaca, headed by Glavocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did it represent the civilian authorities or was this something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It should have represented the civilian authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Talking about civilian authorities, do you know that those civilian authorities, regardless how we called them, whether we use the term that you are using or my term, the government of Busovaca, that certain Muslims stayed on working there, not just as ordinary employees but as functionaries in addition to Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Since the takeover of power by the HVO, there was no room for any Muslim any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What about Nezir Huseinspahic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Well, come on, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, he stayed on in the HVO government, for much of 1992. Please answer my question "Yes" or "No".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean. Husein? Could you repeat the name, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Nezir Huseinspahic. I hope I got the name right. I think he was in charge of general administrative affairs. Let me give you another name then. The head of Kadasta (phoen) was Mrs. Alema, a Muslim lady.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Then Mrs. Rizvic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Nobody worked. Not a single person was working. Let's get this right. This Alema that you mentioned, her mother was killed. When everything stopped, her mother was killed. Nobody was working.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you're saying the people whose names I mentioned did not stay on working in the civilian authorities of the HVO after May 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Out of the question. That's ridiculous.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: When we were talking about those bodies, do you know, from the municipal assembly formed after the first elections, that a body emerged from it, it was called the crisis staff, before the civilian HVO government was formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know who was the president of that crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Maybe I misnamed it. Maybe that could have been Glavocevic. Maybe I got it wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The crisis staff that we're talking about, the president is Mr. Zoran Maric, ex officio, because he was president of the assembly, the one that was elected after the first elections.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was that the body you had in mind when you referred to the war council?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Zoran Maric came after Glavocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, when we're talking about the military HVO component, do you know who was the commander of the Busovaca HVO, the military commander of the Busovaca HVO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Dario Kordic, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: From the beginning? The first commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: The first and last. Everything was under his control.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I didn't ask you that. I asked who was the commander.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Dario Kordic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Since you lived in Busovaca throughout that time and you know the people, I take it you must know when brigades were formed or, rather, the HVO Brigade in Busovaca. If I understand you well, if Mr. Kordic was the commander of everything, then he must have been the brigade commander as well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Every brigade has its own commander, sir, but then there's the commander above those commanders. You know, there's a hierarchy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But that's precisely what I had in mind and what I asked you first, who is the commander of the HVO in Busovaca, and your answer was Mr. Kordic. There is no scale, no hierarchy, in your answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: There isn't because he is Number 1. Everyone else is below him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Talking about the command and so on, do you know that there was a command for the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Perhaps I heard about that. I may have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You don't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know perhaps who was the commander of the Central Bosnia Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Have you heard of the name Colonel Tihomir Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: In what context? What was he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I know he was a General, that he was mentioned very frequently, and that the people were saying that he should have been the commander of everything, but in reality it wasn't like that, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I'm trying to follow your thoughts. You heard that Mr. Blaskic should have been the commander of the Operative Zone, is that what you've said?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, quite.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you don't know whether he, in fact, was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: On paper he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So your answer to my previous question as to who was the commander of the Operative Zone, you are now saying that on paper it was Mr. Tihimoir Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What was he by occupation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You said in one of your testimonies that he was a professional soldier, an officer of the JNA. So that was his occupation. So we agree that he was a professional soldier. We agree, don't we?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Before passing on to the main issue, Your Honours, I should like to ask how much more time I have left today, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: About 20 minutes. Until half past five, and then you've got tomorrow, but allowing such time for us to have the argument about the dossier and, of course, any cross-examination by Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honours. I'll do my very best to shorten this as much as I can, but this witness has touched on many issues and I really do have quite a lot of questions, but I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, please, a few questions of a different nature. Yesterday you mentioned Mr. Dragutin Zvonimir Cicak, rather, on Thursday, not yesterday, and you said he is your neighbour who has a holiday home some 500 or 600 metres away from your home?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Your house was in the Visovacka (sic) Street? Is that its name? There are two or three streets with the same name. Sorry, Tisovacka. I think Mr. Kordic's street has the same name.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. There was a boulevard and this was Tisovacka Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you say that the distance between your houses was 150 metres. It may be 300, but that's not so important. Those streets linked together to form one, and then the road goes on leading to the village of Ravno and then on to Tisovac. Do we agree?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Where exactly is Mr. Cicak's holiday home? Were those two streets linked up or further away?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, I think it's in the area called Bare, if I'm not mistaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You're referring to Juriceve Bare?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Could I ask the usher for his assistance to show the witness this map? We can use the one that the Prosecutor has tendered, D1870.1. So will you please place it on the ELMO so I can ask the witness a few questions? It's today's map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough, Witness J, to point with the pointer to your house or, rather, Juriceve Bare, on the ELMO, where it says "Busovaca," then the village of Ravan. I think you know the map better than I do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: There is Ravan, here somewhere (Indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So Juriceve Bare is between Busovaca and Ravno?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I should now like to ask you to show us, on the same map, the village of Granice, a little to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Could you move the map a little bit further down, please? Move the map down a little please, Mr. Usher. Move the map down on the ELMO, please. That's fine now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we see the village of Granice. So it's quite to the other side of Busovaca. It's about two and a half or three and a half kilometres from Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Why have I shown you this? Because Mr. Cicak, in his testimony, in his statement, said that he had a weekend home in this village of Granice, which is an entirely different area than Busovaca. Mr. Cicak said this on page 1389 of the transcript, lines 19 to 21. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That's something new to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It's not really for the witness say. It's a matter of comment. You could comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you, Your Honours. I won't be using the map any more. We can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Talking about the wheat in the silo that you mentioned, whose reserves were they, Witness J?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Former Yugoslavia, ex-Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you participate in the negotiations on the way that wheat would be used directly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But you told us that the agreement was to share it 50/50.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Between whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Between the Muslims and the Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You recounted an incident in connection with a truck, but I didn't quite understand your final conclusion. Was that the total quantity of grain and wheat that was shared 50/50 with the Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Who was that grain left to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was left to the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Having mentioned the silo as such, as a name which was meant to be used as a storage place for grain, do you know that in that same silo there was a camp for Croats already in January '93 and onwards?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So it was not a camp there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No. A prison perhaps but not a camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But for whom was it a prison?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Even for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: What do you mean? You mean for soldiers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I too was a soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you make a disciplinary omission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So it must have been something serious when you ended up in prison.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It depends how you look at it. Anyway, I spent six days there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you didn't see civilians there and very poor living conditions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: The conditions were poor, that's quite for sure, for me and for everyone else, but there wasn't a single civilian there and especially not Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell me, please -- I have several questions linked to January 1993. Would you agree with me that the road was cut in the area between Kacuni and Bilalovac in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: What do you mean cut?

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I mean, traffic was blocked. The road was closed to traffic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: It was not possible for vehicles to move along that road, that is, the vehicles of Croats. Until the 25th of January, 1993, it was not blocked. It was blocked towards Zenica. There were obstacles put up there by the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell me, please, you say that you were a civilian in January, 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: As of what date did you become a civilian without any military duties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I had absolutely no military duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But did you have any military assignments in 1992 when you were a member of the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did, to go to the front. I was on the front at Visoko in September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Within which unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: 333rd Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. That's what I was asking. Until when did you act as a soldier in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: For 15 days and then I demobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: And you were not called up again?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell me, please -- I'm talking about the end of 1992 and January of 1993, for the first half -- did the TO have its own units in the town and in the environs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the town, no, only in Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Members of the TO travelled from Busovaca to Kacuni and came back? They went there to work, to put it that way?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Well, tell us then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: We were called in only if there was a need to go to the front, and that was how I was called up in September. We would stay there for about 15 days. We went to Visoko, then after that Maglaj. You would be there for 15 days, return all your weapons that were issued to you, and you'd go back home and nobody would call you up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So there were no armed units of the Patriotic League or the TO in the town of Busovaca in December 1992 and January 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: In the town, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But did they come to town, certain BH army units, under arms? Did they come to town on certain occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. This occurred on the 22nd of January, when Delija was being buried, Mirsad Delija, who was killed on the evening of the 21st. As far as I remember, they performed the honorary salute. Those boys who came went back to Kacuni after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were they local people from the town of Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really cannot remember, but there were people from Kacuni. I think most of them were from Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Tell us, when we're talking about the war against the Serbs, did individuals from Busovaca, early on, participate in the war in Croatia, when the former Yugoslavia, or, rather, the former JNA attacked Croatia? Did people go to Croatia from Busovaca, both Muslims and Croats, to fight the JNA and the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I really cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Would you see people in uniform coming home on leave from Croatia, coming to Busovaca, the town of Busovaca, with military insignia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know, really. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: You never saw anyone coming on leave wearing a uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So let us go on with this topic that I have touched upon, that is, January 1993. When I say that traffic was intercepted on the Kacuni-Bilalovac road for Croats, do you know what happened on the 24th of January, 1993, at around 3.00 in the afternoon in Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, roughly, I do. There was an incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Were you there or do you know from what other people told you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: From other people's stories. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: On that day at the checkpoint at Kacuni, two Croats were killed, Ivica Petrovic and Igor Bogdanovic. They were there in a civilian vehicle. Do you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that a couple of days before that, in that same area, the kidnapping of Ignac Kostroman, one of the leaders of the Croatian people in the area, was attempted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you know nothing about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Excuse me. I just remembered something. You said Mirsad Delija was killed. Was his brother one of the commanders in Kacuni? Does he have a brother?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: He has two brothers.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Was one of them a commander on that roadblock in Kacuni?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably, yes. I don't exclude the possibility, but I'm not sure. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. Talking about this roadblock, and I think we could end with that today, you said on Thursday that you went to Split at the end of 1992 and that you needed a permit, which was signed for you by Niko Grubesic, and you went with that permit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you went to Split. You passed this checkpoint, and I assume you passed through some others when leaving Busovaca. The road was, in fact, scattered with roadblocks in those days, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you needed to have some other kinds of permits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I absolutely needed nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Did you cross a checkpoint held by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So did you have to have some kind of paper, document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So you were allowed to pass?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes. Because if you were going from Busovaca, then you would go to Novi Travnik, Prozor, Jablanica, Metkovic, and Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: The fact that you did not need a permit, as you say, did this apply to both Croats and Muslims? I'm talking about a permit from the BH army.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Generally nobody needed one, that's for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So passage was free?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: If you had that paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: I see in front of me a permit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Perhaps if it's not too late or shall we leave it for tomorrow, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Deal with it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Thank you. Could the usher please distribute copies, one for the witness, for Their Honours and the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: (Interpretation) Please show it to the witness. It's important that he should see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: So we're talking about the same route, Vitez-Prozor. So this is a permit for the passage of persons and vehicles, as it says, issued to Mr. Munib Kajmovic in the TO headquarters, on the 11th of October, 1992, and it is signed by the TO commander in Vitez, Sefkija Dzidic. Have you looked at it, Witness J?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is a permit issued by the Muslim authorities, so to speak, in those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Yes, but of Vitez municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but for passage along the same road that you took as far as Prozor. But you said you didn't need any permit.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: But do you agree that this is a permit for the same stretch of road?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS J (Resumed)
utterances.text: Probably, but I see it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NAUMOVSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll adjourn now until half past two tomorrow. Witness J, would you please be back tomorrow again at half past two, where I hope we'll be able to finish your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
